Loy MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BY AND BETWEEN NASHVILLE AND DAVIDSON COUNTY AREA HOSPITALS AND NASHVILLE FIRE DEPARTMENT EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES AND METROPOLITAN NASHVILLE DEPARTMENT OF EMERGENCY COMMUNICATIONS This MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU) is made and entered into this 15" day of December 2017 by and between NASHVILLE AND DAVIDSON COUNTY AREA HOSPITALS (hereinafter called “Area Hospitals”), and NASHVILLE FIRE DEPARTMENT EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES (hereinafter “NFD EMS”), and METRO NASHVILLE DEPARTMENT OF EMERGENCY COMMUNICATIONS (hereinafter “DEC”). This document replaces any previous MOU regarding the subject of patient transport destination guidelines and diversion guidelines. It is generally recognized that patients should be transported to the closest, most appropriate hospital that can care for their specific condition. Many patients may require treatment at hospitals with special capabilities, i.e. stroke and cardiac centers. It is also recognized that the area hospitals become overwhelmed with patients, exceeding the capacity for physicians and nurses to safely and adequately treat patients. The of this agreement will address destination guidelines and those times requiring hospital diversion. Federal and state transfer requirements, state EMS destination guidelines, and other applicable rules are incorporated into the document. IT IS AGREED: 1 Patient transport guidelines for NFD EMS: A. Patients will be transported to a hospital within the confines of Nashville Davidson County. B, Patients will be transported to the closest, most appropriate facility unless: i, Patient has a physician at a more distant facility. Patients bypassing a closer hospital to travel to a more distant facility due to a physician relationship must have the physician’s name reported to the receiving hospital and recorded on the patient’s EMS record. ii. Patient has a specific condition, i.e. transplant, LVAD, recent postoperative or less than 30 days postpartum, chronic illness, that requires treatment at more distant facility. C. NFD EMS recognizes specialized centers for Trauma, Pediatric Emergency Care, Burn, Chest Pain, Stroke, and Resuscitation Centers. i. Level I and Level II Trauma patients transported per State Trauma Destination Guidelines. ii. Pediatric patients transported per the Pediatric Destination Guidelines. iii. | Burn paticnts transported to the closest designated burn center. ARCHIVE
iv. STEMI patients transported to the closest Chest Pain Center. y. Stroke patients transported to the closest designated Stroke Center. vi. arrest patients having achieved return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) transported to the closest Resuscitation Center. D. Transport veterans directly to Veterans’ Affairs (VA) Hospital upon request.
2. Diversion Guidelines: A, NFD EMS will abide by the declared diversion status of the hospital except as noted elsewhere. B. Advise patient who request to be taken to a facility on diversion that the hospital is unable to accept additional patients, will result in delayed care that can be detrimental to the health and safety of the patient, and the patient cannot be: transported there. C. Type of Diversions: i. Emergency Department (ED) diversion — hospital resources are committed and cannot accept any additional patients STROKE, STEMI, CARDIAC ARREST, and critical TRAUMA patients may still be transported to a hospital that has declared ED diversion if specialized as such ii. Obstetrical (OB) diversion iii, Stroke iv. STEMI v. Trauma vi. Total diversion — the intent is to stop all patient transports; when declaring TOTAL diversion, the hospital must qualify the reason for diversion, i.e. HazMat, power failure, water outage, bomb threat, etc. D. NFD EMS will honor diversion status, Exceptions are: i. Patient is unstable with unmanageable airway or hemorrhage. ii, Patient has physician at hospital on diversion status. iii, Patient has specific condition, i.e. transplant, LVAD, recent postoperative or less than 30 days postpartum, or chronic illness requiring treatment at diversion hospital. E. EMS Chief may cancel ED diversion when three or more hospitals are on diversions. The hospital must remain off diversion for at least two hours thereafter. F. Diversion status will be cancelled if a Mass Casualty Incident (MCI) has been declared by the EMS Chief.
3. The Metro Nashville Department of Emergency Communications (DEC) shall: A. Receive phone calls from the area hospitals regarding diversion status. B. Enter diversion information, type of diversion and caller’s name, into computer aided dispatch (CAD) software. C. Notify NFD EMS units and hospitals of the status of hospitals on diversion. ARCHIV E
4. Area Hospitals shall: A. Determine and establish their own internal, written policies and procedures regarding census levels and what may constitute their facility requiring a request for diversion status. B. Have a diversion avoidance protocol. C. Designate appropriate and consistent personnel to contact ECC regarding diversion status. D. Honor current transfer agreements / mutual aid agreements. E. Comply with state transfer regulations, state EMS destination guidelines, EMTALA, and provider/payor requirements. F. Consider hospital diversion only after the hospital has exhausted all internal mechanisms to relieve the overcrowding sitiation, due to concern for public safety and the potential for limiting the ability of NFD EMS to respond to 911 emergency calls, G. Limit periods of diversion to four hour blocks of time. Another period of diversion must involve a status reassessment. H, In cases of extended diversion, i.e. greater than four hours, contact the ECC to provide confirmation of the hospital’s status. I. Hospitals going on diversion status must do so prior to being notified of an impending arrival of a NFD EMS transport unit; there shall be no “diversions while enroute.” J. Notify NFD EMS of any changes in a hospital’s capabilities, i.e. changes in accreditation of stroke center or chest pain center status, no longer accepting OB or pediatrics; etc.
5. Nashville Fire Department Emergency Medical Services (NFD EMS) shall: A. Provide its personnel a detailed policy regarding the specifics of this MOU and it shall be incorporated into the department’s Operational Procedures and Guidelines (OPG). B. Provide its ambulance crews a means to receive hospital diversion status, i.e. pager, text alerts, etc. C. Compile a monthly report of all hospital diversions and forward to all area hospitals.
6. Oversight committee shall: A. Be comprised of the following: i. Representative from each area hospital Emergency Department ii. Hospital administrator, or appointee, from each area hospital iii. | NFD Director Chief or appointee iv. NFD EMS Chief vy. Nashville Fire Department Medical Director or Assistant Medical Director ~ vi. Department of Emergency Communications director or appointee vii. | Other members as necessary B. Meet quarterly. ARCHIV
C. Debrief and critique all diversions, D. Make recommendations for further enhancements of process. E, Determine if there are consequences for non-compliance. Definitions: A. Chest Pain Center — certified by Society of Cardiovascular Patient Care or Joint Commission B. Stroke Center — certified by Joint Commission C. Pediatric Destination Guidelines — all children deemed critically ill, potentially seriously ill, or with special health care needs should be transported to the closest, most appropriate pediatric emergency department or the pediatric emergency department requested by the parents or guardian. Pediatric patients in arrest shall be transported to the closest pediatric emergency department as long as the patient can.be effectively ventilated. Those children post-arrest having a pulse restored shall be transported to the closest pediatric emergency department. Pediatric trauma patients shall be transported per state EMS destination guidelines. D. Resuscitation Center — facility committing to rapid transport to cardiac catheterization lab for cardiac arrest patient achieving ROSC and then initiating targeted temperature management therapy for VF/VT patients achieving ROSC who do not respond in a meaningful way to verbal stimuli. This memorandum may be terminated by either party at any time upon thirty days written notice. ARCHIVE
